{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JGMChxGj8bGAwMymSMZ3oF","type":"tool_result","content":"Web search results for query: \"Node.js 25 localStorage global \"getItem is not a function\" Next.js prerender\"\n\nLinks: [{\"title\":\"[Bug]: localStorage.getItem is not a function on Node.js 25+ (window = globalThis breaks SSR guard) · Issue #389 · pacocoursey/next-themes\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes/issues/389\"},{\"title\":\"Cause and Fix for `localStorage.getItem is not a function` Error in Next.js 15 | Digital Archive Systems Tech Blog\",\"url\":\"https://tech.ldas.jp/en/posts/36e5d3a653a809/\"},{\"title\":\"localStorage is not defined - Next.js · vercel/next.js · Discussion #19911\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/19911\"},{\"title\":\"How to Fix “localStorage is not defined” in Next.js | by Zamin Mirzad | Medium\",\"url\":\"https://medium.com/@zamin_mirzad/how-to-fix-localstorage-is-not-defined-in-next-js-b237498d12ce\"},{\"title\":\"ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined in Next.js: Causes and How – Omi AI\",\"url\":\"https://www.omi.me/blogs/next-js-errors/referenceerror-localstorage-is-not-defined-in-next-js-causes-and-how-to-fix\"},{\"title\":\"⨯ [TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function] - Help - Vercel Community\",\"url\":\"https://community.vercel.com/t/typeerror-localstorage-getitem-is-not-a-function/28578\"},{\"title\":\"github.com\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript-Website/pull/3450\"},{\"title\":\"ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined in Next.js\",\"url\":\"https://sentry.io/answers/referenceerror-localstorage-is-not-defined-in-next-js/\"},{\"title\":\"github.com\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/kubestellar/docs/pull/425\"}]\n\nI've found comprehensive information about this issue. Here's a summary of the search results:\n\n## The Problem\n\nNode.js 25 breaks the traditional SSR guard by aliasing `window` to `globalThis`, which is defined in all environments, and ships an experimental implementation of the Web Storage API where `window` is defined as an alias for `globalThis`.\n\nIn Node.js 24 and earlier, `globalThis.localStorage` was undefined so the guard `typeof localStorage !== 'undefined'` worked correctly, but in Node.js 25, the localStorage object exists, so the guard is bypassed. When getItem is called, the method is undefined, resulting in TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function.\n\n## The Root Cause\n\nIn Node.js 25, the `globalThis.localStorage` object exists by default, but without specifying a valid file path with the `--localstorage-file` flag, the localStorage object itself exists but methods like getItem and setItem do not function – a half-working state.\n\n## The Solution\n\nThe fix should use `typeof globalThis.document` or `typeof globalThis.localStorage` as guards instead of `typeof window`, since `document` and a complete `localStorage` remain browser-only APIs.\n\nThis is particularly relevant for Next.js 15 with Node.js 25+, as Next.js 15's internal code and dependency libraries use this pattern, causing errors during server-side rendering.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5808fab8-1233-4afd-bd25-658456e4faf2","uuid":"b93e7803-c709-4655-bce7-6f7e739b4eb2","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:42:54.932Z","tool_use_result":{"query":"Node.js 25 localStorage global \"getItem is not a function\" Next.js prerender","results":[{"tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_01P6kmkaLFArmNL8FY81Bnbo","content":[{"title":"[Bug]: localStorage.getItem is not a function on Node.js 25+ (window = globalThis breaks SSR guard) · Issue #389 · pacocoursey/next-themes","url":"https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes/issues/389"},{"title":"Cause and Fix for `localStorage.getItem is not a function` Error in Next.js 15 | Digital Archive Systems Tech Blog","url":"https://tech.ldas.jp/en/posts/36e5d3a653a809/"},{"title":"localStorage is not defined - Next.js · vercel/next.js · Discussion #19911","url":"https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/19911"},{"title":"How to Fix “localStorage is not defined” in Next.js | by Zamin Mirzad | Medium","url":"https://medium.com/@zamin_mirzad/how-to-fix-localstorage-is-not-defined-in-next-js-b237498d12ce"},{"title":"ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined in Next.js: Causes and How – Omi AI","url":"https://www.omi.me/blogs/next-js-errors/referenceerror-localstorage-is-not-defined-in-next-js-causes-and-how-to-fix"},{"title":"⨯ [TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function] - Help - Vercel Community","url":"https://community.vercel.com/t/typeerror-localstorage-getitem-is-not-a-function/28578"},{"title":"github.com","url":"https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript-Website/pull/3450"},{"title":"ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined in Next.js","url":"https://sentry.io/answers/referenceerror-localstorage-is-not-defined-in-next-js/"},{"title":"github.com","url":"https://github.com/kubestellar/docs/pull/425"}]},"I've found comprehensive information about this issue. Here's a summary of the search results:\n\n## The Problem\n\nNode.js 25 breaks the traditional SSR guard by aliasing `window` to `globalThis`, which is defined in all environments, and ships an experimental implementation of the Web Storage API where `window` is defined as an alias for `globalThis`.\n\nIn Node.js 24 and earlier, `globalThis.localStorage` was undefined so the guard `typeof localStorage !== 'undefined'` worked correctly, but in Node.js 25, the localStorage object exists, so the guard is bypassed. When getItem is called, the method is undefined, resulting in TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function.\n\n## The Root Cause\n\nIn Node.js 25, the `globalThis.localStorage` object exists by default, but without specifying a valid file path with the `--localstorage-file` flag, the localStorage object itself exists but methods like getItem and setItem do not function – a half-working state.\n\n## The Solution\n\nThe fix should use `typeof globalThis.document` or `typeof globalThis.localStorage` as guards instead of `typeof window`, since `document` and a complete `localStorage` remain browser-only APIs.\n\nThis is particularly relevant for Next.js 15 with Node.js 25+, as Next.js 15's internal code and dependency libraries use this pattern, causing errors during server-side rendering."],"durationSeconds":8.313399915999995,"searchCount":1}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMDYivQcR28znNMM4Azq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QZspuSFnSDNgPLK9y8WRgM","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /tmp\necho \"== can we disable it? ==\"\nnode --no-experimental-webstorage -e \"console.log('typeof:', typeof localStorage)\" 2>&1 | head -3\necho \"== with a real file, does getItem work? ==\"\nnode --localstorage-file=./ls.tmp -e \"console.log('getItem:', typeof localStorage.getItem); localStorage.setItem('a','1'); console.log('read:', localStorage.getItem('a'))\" 2>&1 | head -5\necho \"== does reassigning the global work? ==\"\nnode -e \"globalThis.localStorage = {getItem:()=>null}; console.log('after reassign getItem:', typeof localStorage.getItem)\" 2>&1 | head -3\necho \"== is the property configurable/writable? ==\"\nnode -e \"console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis,'localStorage'))\" 2>&1 | head -8","description":"Test disabling webstorage, file backing, and reassignment"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1887,"cache_read_input_tokens":18037,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1887,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5808fab8-1233-4afd-bd25-658456e4faf2","uuid":"7394f19e-4ffe-4ceb-a7b0-e3e87b602dc6","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:43:31.700Z","request_id":"req_011CdMDYhsuKSTrDYmtEwdXD"}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XXqrPVkcHhoXLCZKEqJkX3","type":"tool_result","content":"# Root Cause Analysis: Node.js 25 localStorage Issue\n\n## The Core Problem\n\nNode.js 25 introduced an experimental Web Storage API that aliases `window` to `globalThis`. This breaks the traditional SSR detection pattern used by next-themes:\n\n**Why it fails:**\n- The check `typeof window == \"undefined\"` evaluates to `false` on the Node.js server (since `window` now exists as an alias)\n- next-themes then attempts to call `localStorage.getItem()` during server-side execution\n- Node.js 25's partial localStorage implementation lacks proper `getItem` support\n- Result: `TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`\n\n## Why Polyfills Don't Help\n\nInstrumentation-based polyfills cannot fix the prerender phase because the check occurs at **module load time** before instrumentation runs. The boolean flag (`J = false`) is cached before any monkey-patching can take effect.\n\n## Recommended Fix\n\nReplace the outdated guard with a more robust check:\n\n**Use `typeof globalThis.document` or `typeof globalThis.localStorage`** as the SSR detection mechanism, since these remain genuinely browser-only APIs that won't exist on the Node.js server.\n\nThe issue states: *\"document and a complete localStorage remain browser-only APIs,\"* making them reliable alternatives to the `window` check that now fails in Node.js 25+."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5808fab8-1233-4afd-bd25-658456e4faf2","uuid":"932fe1c4-0639-4994-89c9-a5f162436c68","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:43:40.269Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":264053,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# Root Cause Analysis: Node.js 25 localStorage Issue\n\n## The Core Problem\n\nNode.js 25 introduced an experimental Web Storage API that aliases `window` to `globalThis`. This breaks the traditional SSR detection pattern used by next-themes:\n\n**Why it fails:**\n- The check `typeof window == \"undefined\"` evaluates to `false` on the Node.js server (since `window` now exists as an alias)\n- next-themes then attempts to call `localStorage.getItem()` during server-side execution\n- Node.js 25's partial localStorage implementation lacks proper `getItem` support\n- Result: `TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`\n\n## Why Polyfills Don't Help\n\nInstrumentation-based polyfills cannot fix the prerender phase because the check occurs at **module load time** before instrumentation runs. The boolean flag (`J = false`) is cached before any monkey-patching can take effect.\n\n## Recommended Fix\n\nReplace the outdated guard with a more robust check:\n\n**Use `typeof globalThis.document` or `typeof globalThis.localStorage`** as the SSR detection mechanism, since these remain genuinely browser-only APIs that won't exist on the Node.js server.\n\nThe issue states: *\"document and a complete localStorage remain browser-only APIs,\"* making them reliable alternatives to the `window` check that now fails in Node.js 25+.","durationMs":6264,"url":"https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes/issues/389"}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMDecNvk3g8oJWw2GW2J","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MAeVp5zoCV2nUypZZFnX1i","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-quiz-004/2026-07-24T164143Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why the Scaffold-ETH 2 static export broke on Node 25\n\n## TL;DR\n\nNode 25 ships the experimental **Web Storage API on by default**. That means\n`localStorage` (and `sessionStorage`) now exist as *globals* in plain Node — but\nwithout a `--localstorage-file` they are **half-initialized stubs**: the object\nexists (`{}`), yet its methods (`getItem`, `setItem`, …) are never wired up.\n\nSo the classic browser-detection guard `typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"`\n**now passes on the server**, the code walks straight into\n`localStorage.getItem(...)`, and `getItem` is `undefined` →\n`TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`.\n\n- **Teammate A** is running a pre-Node-22 mental model. Node *does* have\n  `localStorage` now.\n- **Teammate B**'s polyfill can't win because the failing check runs at\n  **module-evaluation time inside the prerender workers**, before\n  `instrumentation.ts` ever executes — the wrong phase and, for build workers,\n  the wrong process. A perfect polyfill that runs too late is inert.\n- **The fix** is to stop pretending it's a browser: disable Node's Web Storage\n  for the build (`--no-experimental-webstorage`), and/or pin CI back to Node 24\n  until dependencies fix their guards. Root cause for code you own: guard on\n  `typeof globalThis.document`, not on `window`/`localStorage`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What actually changed in Node\n\nNode added a WHATWG **Web Storage** implementation:\n\n- **Node 22.4.0** — `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` introduced as globals, but\n  gated behind the `--experimental-webstorage` flag. If you didn't pass the\n  flag, they didn't exist, so nothing broke.\n- **Node 25** — Web Storage is **enabled by default**. No flag required. This is\n  the line CI just crossed when it moved from 24 → 25.\n\nI reproduced this on the exact runtime CI is now using (`node v25.9.0`):\n\n```\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof localStorage)\"\nobject                       # <-- it EXISTS now\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(localStorage)\"\n{}                           # <-- but it's an empty, half-built object\n(node:xxxxx) Warning: `--localstorage-file` was provided without a valid path\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof localStorage.getItem)\"\nundefined                    # <-- so its methods are NOT functions\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof sessionStorage)\"\nobject                       # same story for sessionStorage\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof window)\"\nundefined                    # window is still NOT defined in Node 25.9.0\n```\n\nTwo things matter here:\n\n1. `localStorage` is now a **truthy, defined global** on the server.\n2. Until you point Node at a backing store with `--localstorage-file`, it's a\n   **stub with no working methods**. Providing a valid file makes the methods\n   real:\n\n   ```\n   $ node --localstorage-file=./ls.tmp -e \"localStorage.setItem('a','1'); console.log(localStorage.getItem('a'))\"\n   1                          # getItem is a real function once a file is set\n   ```\n\n(Note: some write-ups also claim Node 25 aliases `window` to `globalThis`. That\ndid **not** reproduce on 25.9.0 here — `typeof window` is still `undefined`. The\nthing that actually broke your build is the `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`\nglobals, so that's what the rest of this focuses on.)\n\n## 2. The exact mechanism of your error\n\nScaffold-ETH 2's provider stack (wagmi / RainbowKit / theme + Zustand `persist`\nstores) is full of storage-backed code guarded by browser checks like:\n\n```js\nconst isBrowser = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\";\n// ...later...\nconst raw = localStorage.getItem(KEY);\n```\n\nWalk it through on each runtime:\n\n| Runtime | `typeof localStorage` | Guard result | `localStorage.getItem` | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Real browser | `\"object\"` (working) | browser ✓ | function | fine |\n| Node ≤ 24 | `\"undefined\"` | server ✓ (skips) | n/a | fine |\n| **Node 25** | `\"object\"` (**stub**) | **browser ✗** (falls through) | **undefined** | **`getItem is not a function`** |\n\nThe guard was never designed to distinguish \"real browser Storage\" from \"Node's\nempty Storage stub.\" Node 25 introduced a third state the guard can't see, and\nthe guard guesses wrong.\n\n`/_not-found` is just the first page Next tries to prerender. It's the built-in\n404, but it still renders through your root layout and provider tree, so it's the\nfirst page to touch storage during static export. Any page would trip the same\nway.\n\n## 3. Why Teammate A is wrong\n\nA's claim — \"Node has no `localStorage`, so there's nothing to call `getItem`\non\" — was **correct up to and including Node 24**. It's now stale by exactly one\nmajor version.\n\nNotice A's model predicts the *opposite* symptom. If `localStorage` truly didn't\nexist, you'd get `ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined` (or the guard\nwould short-circuit and you'd get nothing at all). You are instead getting a\n`TypeError` about a **missing method on an existing object**. That error is only\npossible if `localStorage` *is* defined — which is precisely the Node 25 change\nA hasn't absorbed. The error isn't impossible; it's the fingerprint of the new\nbehavior.\n\n## 4. Why Teammate B's fix cannot work — where the prerender actually runs\n\nB's instinct (\"localStorage is broken → give it a correct polyfill\") is aimed at\nthe wrong problem and, more importantly, fires in the wrong place.\n\n**Where does the prerender run?** Not in the browser, and not in the long-lived\nNext server that `instrumentation.ts` is built for. Static export (`next build`)\nrenders your pages in **Node, inside Next's build/prerender worker processes** —\nit spins up worker processes that `import` your page/layout module graph and\nexecute it to produce HTML. The `TypeError` is thrown *there*, in a Node worker,\nat render time.\n\n`instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` is the hook for a **running server\ninstance** starting up. Against those build-time prerender workers it loses for\ntwo independent reasons:\n\n1. **Wrong phase (the decisive one).** The offending browser-detection runs at\n   **module-evaluation time** — the instant the worker imports the module. Many\n   of these libraries compute the decision *once* and cache it, e.g.\n   `const isBrowser = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"` at module top level,\n   or they call `localStorage.getItem` directly while the module initializes its\n   store. By the time any `register()` polyfill could run, the guard has already\n   evaluated (and frozen) its answer and/or the failing call has already\n   happened. You cannot monkey-patch a global *before* code that read it during\n   its own import.\n\n2. **Wrong process / not guaranteed to run.** `instrumentation.register()` is\n   not a reliable \"runs first in every prerender worker\" pre-hook. The isolated\n   render workers evaluate your page modules to emit HTML; the instrumentation\n   polyfill isn't guaranteed to have executed in that worker before those\n   modules load.\n\nAnd note what B is even trying to do: **supply a missing global**. But nothing\nis missing — Node *already* defined `localStorage`. The global property is\nwritable/configurable (I checked: it has a get/set descriptor and reassigning\n`globalThis.localStorage = {...}` *does* take effect), so overriding it is\ntechnically possible. The barrier is purely **timing**: to win, your override\nhas to run before the first guard/first access in that worker, and\n`instrumentation.ts` categorically does not give you that ordering during a\nstatic export.\n\nThat's why \"no matter how correct the polyfill is\" holds: correctness of the\npolyfill is irrelevant when it never runs before the code it's meant to protect.\n\n## 5. What actually fixes it\n\nRanked, most robust / least effort first. For a Scaffold-ETH app you don't own\nthe guard code inside `next-themes`, wagmi, Zustand persist, etc., so prefer the\nenvironment-level fixes:\n\n1. **Turn Node's Web Storage back off for the build** (best targeted fix —\n   restores the exact environment your deps expect, no code changes):\n\n   ```bash\n   # in the CI build step / package.json script\n   NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage yarn build\n   ```\n\n   Verified on 25.9.0:\n\n   ```\n   $ node --no-experimental-webstorage -e \"console.log(typeof localStorage)\"\n   undefined\n   ```\n\n   With the global gone, `typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"` correctly reports\n   \"server\" again and every one of those guards skips as before. This fixes it\n   regardless of *which* dependency has the sloppy guard.\n\n2. **Pin CI back to Node 24 LTS** (fastest unblock while you roll out the above\n   or wait on upstream). Set it in your CI matrix / `.nvmrc` / `engines`. Node 24\n   doesn't ship Web Storage by default, so the regression disappears.\n\n3. **Fix the guard at the root** (for code you own or can patch/override). Detect\n   the browser with something that is *still* browser-only in Node 25:\n\n   ```js\n   // ❌ both now unreliable on the server in Node 25\n   const isBrowser = typeof window !== \"undefined\";\n   const isBrowser = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\";\n\n   // ✅ document has no Node global; use it (or feature-detect a WORKING storage)\n   const isBrowser =\n     typeof globalThis.document !== \"undefined\" &&\n     typeof globalThis.localStorage?.getItem === \"function\";\n   ```\n\n   Then bump/patch the dependencies that had the bad guard (e.g. update\n   `next-themes` to a release that fixed this; similar fixes are landing across\n   the ecosystem).\n\nFor a Scaffold-ETH 2 monorepo, do **#1 in CI now** (one-line, unblocks the\nexport), keep **#2** as the safety net, and track **#3** via dependency upgrades\nso you can eventually drop the flag and move forward on Node 25+.\n\n## 6. What NOT to do\n\n- **Don't give the build a `--localstorage-file`.** It *would* stop the crash\n  (`getItem` becomes a real function, verified above), but you'd be handing your\n  prerender a persistent, file-backed \"browser\" storage that has no business\n  existing during static generation. It masks the real bug — a browser/server\n  detection failure — instead of fixing it, and invites subtly wrong prerendered\n  output.\n- **Don't add more polyfills in `instrumentation.ts`** (B's path). Same phase/\n  process problem described in §4 — it can't run early enough for the prerender\n  workers.\n- **Don't `try/catch` around every storage access.** It buries the signal and\n  leaves the persist/theme logic silently no-op'ing during prerender.\n\n---\n\n## Sources\n\n- [Node.js 25 `localStorage.getItem is not a function` — next-themes issue #389](https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes/issues/389)\n- [Cause and Fix for `localStorage.getItem is not a function` in Next.js 15](https://tech.ldas.jp/en/posts/36e5d3a653a809/)\n- [TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function — Vercel Community](https://community.vercel.com/t/typeerror-localstorage-getitem-is-not-a-function/28578)\n- Directly reproduced on `node v25.9.0` (probes shown inline above).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2423,"cache_read_input_tokens":23195,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2423,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5808fab8-1233-4afd-bd25-658456e4faf2","uuid":"c51f55d6-7f5b-4662-b697-39ede9b621e1","timestamp":"2026-07-24T16:45:31.962Z","request_id":"req_011CdMDeaAE6gk2bYN1yXKSh"}

That means\n`localStorage` (and `sessionStorage`) now exist as *globals* in plain Node — but\nwithout a `--localstorage-file` they are **half-initialized stubs**: the object\nexists (`{}`), yet its methods (`getItem`, `setItem`, …) are never wired up.\n\nSo the classic browser-detection guard `typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"`\n**now passes on the server**, the code walks straight into\n`localStorage.getItem(...)`, and `getItem` is `undefined` →\n`TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`.\n\n- **Teammate A** is running a pre-Node-22 mental model. Node *does* have\n  `localStorage` now.\n- **Teammate B**'s polyfill can't win because the failing check runs at\n  **module-evaluation time inside the prerender workers**, before\n  `instrumentation.ts` ever executes — the wrong phase and, for build workers,\n  the wrong process. A perfect polyfill that runs too late is inert.\n- **The fix** is to stop pretending it's a browser: disable Node's Web Storage\n  for the build (`--no-experimental-webstorage`), and/or pin CI back to Node 24\n  until dependencies fix their guards. Root cause for code you own: guard on\n  `typeof globalThis.document`, not on `window`/`localStorage`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What actually changed in Node\n\nNode added a WHATWG **Web Storage** implementation:\n\n- **Node 22.4.0** — `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` introduced as globals, but\n  gated behind the `--experimental-webstorage` flag. If you didn't pass the\n  flag, they didn't exist, so nothing broke.\n- **Node 25** — Web Storage is **enabled by default**. No flag required. This is\n  the line CI just crossed when it moved from 24 → 25.\n\nI reproduced this on the exact runtime CI is now using (`node v25.9.0`):\n\n```\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof localStorage)\"\nobject                       # <-- it EXISTS now\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(localStorage)\"\n{}                           # <-- but it's an empty, half-built object\n(node:xxxxx) Warning: `--localstorage-file` was provided without a valid path\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof localStorage.getItem)\"\nundefined                    # <-- so its methods are NOT functions\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof sessionStorage)\"\nobject                       # same story for sessionStorage\n\n$ node -e \"console.log(typeof window)\"\nundefined                    # window is still NOT defined in Node 25.9.0\n```\n\nTwo things matter here:\n\n1. `localStorage` is now a **truthy, defined global** on the server.\n2. Until you point Node at a backing store with `--localstorage-file`, it's a\n   **stub with no working methods**. Providing a valid file makes the methods\n   real:\n\n   ```\n   $ node --localstorage-file=./ls.tmp -e \"localStorage.setItem('a','1'); console.log(localStorage.getItem('a'))\"\n   1                          # getItem is a real function once a file is set\n   ```\n\n(Note: some write-ups also claim Node 25 aliases `window` to `globalThis`. That\ndid **not** reproduce on 25.9.0 here — `typeof window` is still `undefined`. The\nthing that actually broke your build is the `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`\nglobals, so that's what the rest of this focuses on.)\n\n## 2. The exact mechanism of your error\n\nScaffold-ETH 2's provider stack (wagmi / RainbowKit / theme + Zustand `persist`\nstores) is full of storage-backed code guarded by browser checks like:\n\n```js\nconst isBrowser = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\";\n// ...later...\nconst raw = localStorage.getItem(KEY);\n```\n\nWalk it through on each runtime:\n\n| Runtime | `typeof localStorage` | Guard result | `localStorage.getItem` | Outcome |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Real browser | `\"object\"` (working) | browser ✓ | function | fine |\n| Node ≤ 24 | `\"undefined\"` | server ✓ (skips) | n/a | fine |\n| **Node 25** | `\"object\"` (**stub**) | **browser ✗** (falls through) | **undefined** | **`getItem is not a function`** |\n\nThe guard was never designed to distinguish \"real browser Storage\" from \"Node's\nempty Storage stub.\" Node 25 introduced a third state the guard can't see, and\nthe guard guesses wrong.\n\n`/_not-found` is just the first page Next tries to prerender. It's the built-in\n404, but it still renders through your root layout and provider tree, so it's the\nfirst page to touch storage during static export. Any page would trip the same\nway.\n\n## 3. Why Teammate A is wrong\n\nA's claim — \"Node has no `localStorage`, so there's nothing to call `getItem`\non\" — was **correct up to and including Node 24**. It's now stale by exactly one\nmajor version.\n\nNotice A's model predicts the *opposite* symptom. If `localStorage` truly didn't\nexist, you'd get `ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined` (or the guard\nwould short-circuit and you'd get nothing at all). You are instead getting a\n`TypeError` about a **missing method on an existing object**. That error is only\npossible if `localStorage` *is* defined — which is precisely the Node 25 change\nA hasn't absorbed. The error isn't impossible; it's the fingerprint of the new\nbehavior.\n\n## 4. Why Teammate B's fix cannot work — where the prerender actually runs\n\nB's instinct (\"localStorage is broken → give it a correct polyfill\") is aimed at\nthe wrong problem and, more importantly, fires in the wrong place.\n\n**Where does the prerender run?** Not in the browser, and not in the long-lived\nNext server that `instrumentation.ts` is built for. Static export (`next build`)\nrenders your pages in **Node, inside Next's build/prerender worker processes** —\nit spins up worker processes that `import` your page/layout module graph and\nexecute it to produce HTML. The `TypeError` is thrown *there*, in a Node worker,\nat render time.\n\n`instrumentation.ts`'s `register()` is the hook for a **running server\ninstance** starting up. Against those build-time prerender workers it loses for\ntwo independent reasons:\n\n1. **Wrong phase (the decisive one).** The offending browser-detection runs at\n   **module-evaluation time** — the instant the worker imports the module. Many\n   of these libraries compute the decision *once* and cache it, e.g.\n   `const isBrowser = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"` at module top level,\n   or they call `localStorage.getItem` directly while the module initializes its\n   store. By the time any `register()` polyfill could run, the guard has already\n   evaluated (and frozen) its answer and/or the failing call has already\n   happened. You cannot monkey-patch a global *before* code that read it during\n   its own import.\n\n2. **Wrong process / not guaranteed to run.** `instrumentation.register()` is\n   not a reliable \"runs first in every prerender worker\" pre-hook. The isolated\n   render workers evaluate your page modules to emit HTML; the instrumentation\n   polyfill isn't guaranteed to have executed in that worker before those\n   modules load.\n\nAnd note what B is even trying to do: **supply a missing global**. But nothing\nis missing — Node *already* defined `localStorage`. The global property is\nwritable/configurable (I checked: it has a get/set descriptor and reassigning\n`globalThis.localStorage = {...}` *does* take effect), so overriding it is\ntechnically possible. The barrier is purely **timing**: to win, your override\nhas to run before the first guard/first access in that worker, and\n`instrumentation.ts` categorically does not give you that ordering during a\nstatic export.\n\nThat's why \"no matter how correct the polyfill is\" holds: correctness of the\npolyfill is irrelevant when it never runs before the code it's meant to protect.\n\n## 5. What actually fixes it\n\nRanked, most robust / least effort first. For a Scaffold-ETH app you don't own\nthe guard code inside `next-themes`, wagmi, Zustand persist, etc., so prefer the\nenvironment-level fixes:\n\n1. **Turn Node's Web Storage back off for the build** (best targeted fix —\n   restores the exact environment your deps expect, no code changes):\n\n   ```bash\n   # in the CI build step / package.json script\n   NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage yarn build\n   ```\n\n   Verified on 25.9.0:\n\n   ```\n   $ node --no-experimental-webstorage -e \"console.log(typeof localStorage)\"\n   undefined\n   ```\n\n   With the global gone, `typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"` correctly reports\n   \"server\" again and every one of those guards skips as before. This fixes it\n   regardless of *which* dependency has the sloppy guard.\n\n2. **Pin CI back to Node 24 LTS** (fastest unblock while you roll out the above\n   or wait on upstream). Set it in your CI matrix / `.nvmrc` / `engines`. Node 24\n   doesn't ship Web Storage by default, so the regression disappears.\n\n3. **Fix the guard at the root** (for code you own or can patch/override). Detect\n   the browser with something that is *still* browser-only in Node 25:\n\n   ```js\n   // ❌ both now unreliable on the server in Node 25\n   const isBrowser = typeof window !== \"undefined\";\n   const isBrowser = typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\";\n\n   // ✅ document has no Node global; use it (or feature-detect a WORKING storage)\n   const isBrowser =\n     typeof globalThis.document !== \"undefined\" &&\n     typeof globalThis.localStorage?.getItem === \"function\";\n   ```\n\n   Then bump/patch the dependencies that had the bad guard (e.g. update\n   `next-themes` to a release that fixed this; similar fixes are landing across\n   the ecosystem).\n\nFor a Scaffold-ETH 2 monorepo, do **#1 in CI now** (one-line, unblocks the\nexport), keep **#2** as the safety net, and track **#3** via dependency upgrades\nso you can eventually drop the flag and move forward on Node 25+.\n\n## 6. What NOT to do\n\n- **Don't give the build a `--localstorage-file`.** It *would* stop the crash\n  (`getItem` becomes a real function, verified above), but you'd be handing your\n  prerender a persistent, file-backed \"browser\" storage that has no business\n  existing during static generation. It masks the real bug — a browser/server\n  detection failure — instead of fixing it, and invites subtly wrong prerendered\n  output.\n- **Don't add more polyfills in `instrumentation.ts`** (B's path). Same phase/\n  process problem described in §4 — it can't run early enough for the prerender\n  workers.\n- **Don't `try/catch` around every storage access.** It buries the signal and\n  leaves the persist/theme logic silently no-op'ing during prerender.\n\n---\n\n## Sources\n\n- [Node.js 25 `localStorage.getItem is not a function` — next-themes issue #389](https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes/issues/389)\n- [Cause and Fix for `localStorage.getItem is not a function` in Next.js 15](https://tech.ldas.jp/en/posts/36e5d3a653a809/)\n- [TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function — Vercel Community](https://community.vercel.com/t/typeerror-localstorage-getitem-is-not-a-function/28578)\n- Directly reproduced on `node v25.9.0` (probes shown inline above).\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
